title: A Letter for the Verdict
premise: In the fading mill town of Harrow's Bend, coroner Dominic Okonkwo is handed a missing-persons case file: schoolteacher Mara Voss, vanished eleven months ago, presumed dead. But when a second diary surfaces in an estate sale, its entries continue past her disappearance — written in a hand that isn't hers, describing deaths only the coroner could verify. As Dominic decodes the ledger of names hidden in the diary's margins, they discover Mara faked her death to escape a trafficking ring protected by the town's founding families, and that the trial of the man she accused will hinge on evidence only Dominic can authenticate. The climax comes at the courthouse, where Dominic must choose between perjury that would free a guilty town and testimony that would doom the woman they have come to love through her pages. In the end, Dominic testifies to the truth, Mara surrenders on her own terms, and both survive — scarred, separated by law, but finally belonging to someone.
about_author: Astrid Villalobos is the pen name of a former rural court stenographer who spent a decade transcribing small-town verdicts and the silences between them. They write mysteries about records, grief, and the people towns decide not to see.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A routine autopsy day establishes Harrow's Bend, Dominic's meticulous care for the dead, and their isolation since their sister left town. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, the comfort of the dead over the living.

chapters.title: The Estate Sale
chapters.summary: Dominic buys a box of books at the Voss house liquidation and finds Mara Voss's diary inside. First entries: warm, funny, observant. Emotional beat: curiosity shading into unease as the last dated entry cuts off mid-sentence.

chapters.title: Eleven Months Cold
chapters.summary: Dominic reviews the official file with Sheriff Ilsa Brandt, who closed the case as a runaway. Flashback texture of Mara's disappearance. Emotional beat: institutional shrug versus Dominic's instinct that something was filed wrong.

chapters.title: The Entry After
chapters.summary: At home, Dominic finds pages bound after the disappearance date — same paper, different hand, describing the condition of a body found in the quarry. A body only Dominic examined. Emotional beat: cold dread; the diary is talking to them.

chapters.title: Quarry Water
chapters.summary: Dominic re-examines the quarry remains' file and finds discrepancies they signed off on under pressure from Brandt. POV alternates with an anonymous diary entry. Emotional beat: guilt; Dominic realizes their own signature may be part of the story.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Margins
chapters.summary: Dominic notices numbers coded into the diary margins — dates, sums, initials. Cross-referencing reveals payments tied to local businesses. Emotional beat: the thrill of pattern recognition curdling into fear of what the pattern means.

chapters.title: Names on the Wall
chapters.summary: Dominic maps the initials onto Harrow's Bend's founding families, including Judge Aldous Crane, presiding over the upcoming trial of dockworker Teo Reyes for manslaughter. Emotional beat: vertigo — the case is bigger than one missing woman.

chapters.title: Teo Reyes, Defendant
chapters.summary: Dominic visits the jail under pretext of a death certificate query. Teo insists he saw Mara alive after her 'disappearance.' Emotional beat: desperate hope; a living witness changes everything.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Diary-voice chapter: the second hand describes watching the river for signs of Mara, revealing the writer loved her too. Dominic reads it at 3 a.m. Emotional beat: tenderness inside menace; the writer is protector or predator.

chapters.title: Brandt's Warning
chapters.summary: Sheriff Brandt tells Dominic to stop pulling threads before trial, revealing she knows more than she says. Emotional beat: threat wrapped in concern; duty and fear shaking hands.

chapters.title: The Second Diary
chapters.summary: A package arrives: another diary, postmarked from out of state, continuing the false-hand narrative and naming the next 'entry' — a person still living in town. Emotional beat: escalation; the diary has become a countdown.

chapters.title: Counting the Living
chapters.summary: Dominic identifies the named person: Ruthie Calloway, a motel clerk who once worked the docks. Dominic warns her; Ruthie denies everything too quickly. Emotional beat: protective urgency meeting terrified denial.

chapters.title: Crane's Courthouse
chapters.summary: Dominic attends a pretrial hearing, observing Judge Crane's control of the room and prosecutor Dana Whitfield's unease. Emotional beat: the machinery of respectability; evil wearing robes.

chapters.title: Mara's Classroom
chapters.summary: Dominic breaks into the sealed Voss house and finds Mara's lesson plans hiding arithmetic matching the ledger. Emotional beat: intimacy with the missing; falling for a mind through its traces.

chapters.title: The Handwriting Question
chapters.summary: Dominic consults an old mentor, forensic document examiner Dr. Priya Nair, who confirms two writers but one intention: the second hand is imitating protection, not committing crime. Emotional beat: ambiguity deepens; the ally may be real.

chapters.title: Ruthie Runs
chapters.summary: Ruthie Calloway vanishes. Brandt calls it coincidence; Dominic doesn't. Emotional beat: failure and fury — warning wasn't enough.

chapters.title: The Ledger Decoded
chapters.summary: Working night and day, Dominic cracks the full cipher: a payment schedule for silence, with Mara's name listed as an asset, not a victim. Emotional beat: horror reframed — Mara may have been complicit, or playing a long game.

chapters.title: Complicity
chapters.summary: Dominic rereads early diary entries with new eyes, finding Mara documenting the ring deliberately, planning exposure. Emotional beat: admiration and heartbreak; she chose this war alone.

chapters.title: Whitfield's Door
chapters.summary: Prosecutor Dana Whitfield privately admits doubts about the case against Teo but fears Crane. She and Dominic form a wary alliance. Emotional beat: two professionals choosing conscience over career.

chapters.title: The Third Entry
chapters.summary: A new diary page arrives naming a date: the first day of trial. The anonymous hand writes, 'Bring the ledger or bury her twice.' Emotional beat: ultimatum; the writer knows Dominic's every move.

chapters.title: Trap or Lifeline
chapters.summary: Dominic and Nair debate whether the correspondent is Mara herself, her lover, or her captor controlling the narrative. Emotional beat: paranoia; every kindness now reads as bait.

chapters.title: Sister's Return
chapters.summary: Dominic's estranged sister Adaeze comes home unexpectedly, probing about the case with questions she shouldn't know to ask. Emotional beat: suspicion infecting family; loneliness weaponized.

chapters.title: Adaeze's Secret
chapters.summary: Confronted, Adaeze admits she works for an investigative nonprofit that flagged Harrow's Bend years ago — and that Mara contacted them before vanishing. Emotional beat: relief and betrayal braided together.

chapters.title: The Docks at Night
chapters.summary: Following ledger coordinates, Dominic photographs active loading activity at the shuttered cannery and is nearly caught. Emotional beat: terror made physical; the town's economy runs on the ring.

chapters.title: Photographs and Leverage
chapters.summary: Whitfield wants the photos for trial; Brandt demands them 'for evidence' — meaning suppression. Dominic must choose a keeper. Emotional beat: the price of trust in a corrupt system.

chapters.title: Ruthie Found
chapters.summary: Ruthie is discovered alive, warehoused in a county facility under a false commitment order signed by Crane. Emotional beat: vindication and rage; the machinery disappears people legally.

chapters.title: The Writer Revealed
chapters.summary: Dominic sets a dead-drop trap using a forged ledger page. The correspondent appears: it is Mara Voss, alive, gaunt, running the long game from the shadows. Emotional beat: shock dissolving into fierce, dangerous joy.

chapters.title: Her Side of the Page
chapters.summary: Mara's POV chapter: how she faked her death with the second diarist — her brother Sami, since killed — and why she needs Dominic's authenticated records to convict Crane. Emotional beat: grief, resolve, and the first honest conversation.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Dominic and Mara spend one stolen day comparing notes and guard down, knowing the trial starts Monday. Emotional beat: love acknowledged precisely because it cannot be kept.

chapters.title: Brandt's Choice
chapters.summary: Dominic confronts Brandt with everything; the sheriff confesses she buried the quarry report to protect her own daughter, whom the ring threatened. Emotional beat: pity without absolution; survival's cost made flesh.

chapters.title: Subpoena
chapters.summary: Whitfield subpoenas Dominic as expert witness on the documents — forcing them to either authenticate the ledger (exposing their chain of custody) or commit perjury. Emotional beat: the trap closes from the righteous side too.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Mara wants to flee; Dominic argues staying is the only way anyone belongs anywhere. They nearly part forever. Emotional beat: the theme stated plainly — love against duty, each demanding sacrifice.

chapters.title: Trial Begins
chapters.summary: Courtroom chapter: Crane steers Teo Reyes's trial toward a fast conviction; Whitfield fights for standing on the diary evidence. Emotional beat: claustrophobic procedure; justice as a narrow door.

chapters.title: The Authentication
chapters.summary: On the stand, Dominic authenticates the ledger truthfully, walking the court through the cipher while Crane tries to discredit their custody chain. Emotional beat: steady courage; the truth delivered like a scalpel.

chapters.title: Crane's Counterstrike
chapters.summary: Crane reveals Mara's staged death, moving to charge her with fraud and paint the ledger as fabrication. Dominic's credibility hangs by a thread. Emotional beat: despair; honesty punished.

chapters.title: Ruthie Takes the Stand
chapters.summary: Ruthie, restored and furious, testifies to the commitment order and the docks. Brandt, unprompted, corroborates the suppressed quarry report. Emotional beat: the dominoes of conscience finally falling.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Teo is acquitted; the grand jury indicts Crane and three founding families. Crane, cornered, all but threatens Dominic in open court — and is arrested within earshot of the gallery. Emotional beat: catharsis earned, not given.

chapters.title: Sentencing of the Living
chapters.summary: Mara turns herself in to negotiate immunity as a cooperating witness; Dominic sits with her through the plea hearing. Emotional beat: bittersweet — survival means surrender, but on her terms.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: Dominic formally corrects the quarry record and holds a small service for Sami Voss and for the town's buried truths. Adaeze stays in Harrow's Bend. Emotional beat: mourning as repair; the dead finally named rightly.

chapters.title: A Letter for the Verdict
chapters.summary: Months later, Mara writes from federal custody; her letter ends mid-sentence exactly where the first diary did — but this time she signs it, and promises a sequel entry. Dominic begins to write back. Emotional beat: belonging chosen; the story continues by consent.
